review_notes: Read the whole file and checked the simp attributes on the mk/inv/mabs, mul/div iff, subgroup, ball, lift and orderHom lemmas. I found no loops or competing rules. The ball/closed-ball membership lemmas are deliberately not simp, because they are proved by simp from `mem_subgroup_iff`. I also checked the downstream uses of the Finite* API in Mathlib/RingTheory/HahnSeries/Lex.lean. The one concrete gap is `FiniteMulArchimedeanClass.mk_le_mk` / `mk_lt_mk`, which are reducing `rfl` lemmas like the simp lemma `val_mk` but are not simp. I did not run Lean, so the effect of adding the attribute on those call sites is untested. `FiniteMulArchimedeanClass.mk_inv` is also not simp although `MulArchimedeanClass.mk_inv` is. I found no downstream use that needs it, so I did not report it.

findings.excerpt: mk a ha ≤ mk b hb ↔ MulArchimedeanClass.mk a ≤ MulArchimedeanClass.mk b := .rfl
findings.problem: These lemmas turn a comparison of `FiniteMulArchimedeanClass.mk` elements into a comparison of ordinary `MulArchimedeanClass.mk` classes. They are proved by `.rfl`, and they are the order-level counterpart of `val_mk`, which is `simp`. They carry no simp attribute, so simp has no rule for `FiniteArchimedeanClass.mk a ha ≤ FiniteArchimedeanClass.mk b hb`. `FiniteMulArchimedeanClass.mk` is a plain `def`, so Subtype order lemmas such as `Subtype.mk_le_mk` will not fire either. The only existing simp rules go through `val`. Downstream code in Mathlib/RingTheory/HahnSeries/Lex.lean therefore calls `rw [FiniteArchimedeanClass.mk_le_mk]` by hand at three sites, in `finiteArchimedeanClassOrderHomLex` and twice in `finiteArchimedeanClassOrderHomInvLex`. The base-class lemmas `mk_le_mk_iff` and `archimedeanClassMk_le_archimedeanClassMk_iff` then apply. The base-class `MulArchimedeanClass.mk_le_mk` and `mk_lt_mk` are also not simp, so this change does not create a competing rule.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both lemmas `@[to_additive (attr := simp)]`. This rewrites the finite-class comparison to the base-class comparison, the same direction as `val_mk`. The right-hand side contains no `FiniteMulArchimedeanClass.mk`, so it cannot loop. Both lemmas have only `a ≠ 1` and `b ≠ 1` as hypotheses, and those are explicit arguments that unify from the expression. The manual `rw [FiniteArchimedeanClass.mk_le_mk]` calls in Lex.lean can then become simp calls.
findings.benefit: Finite-class order goals reduce to the standard `MulArchimedeanClass` API under plain `simp`, as `val_mk` already does for `.val`. Users no longer have to remember to `rw` the bridge lemma by hand.

evidence.excerpt: theorem val_mk {a : M} (h : a ≠ 1) : (mk a h).val = MulArchimedeanClass.mk a := rfl
